questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle Given Its Velocity
questions.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=-2i\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the speed of the particle.
questions.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|-2i| \\  & =|-2| \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

kilometers per hour.

questions.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=(2i-5j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the speed of the particle, rounding your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$

$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
questions.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(5i-3j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i-3j,\,a=i+2j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=2\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i-3j)+(i+2j)(2) \\  & =(5i-3j)+(2i+4j) \\  & =(7i+j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $(3i-8j)\,\text{km/h},$ and when $t=4\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $(15i+8j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.

$a=($
{{field-1}}$\,i$
$+$
{{field-2}}$\,j\,)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=3i-8j,\,v=15i+8j,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 15i+8j & =(3i-8j)+a(4) \\ 12i+16j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(12i+16j) \\  & =(3\,i+4\,j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i+3j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-6i-5j)\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(10i+19j)\,\text{ft/s}.$

$t=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{s}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-6i-5j,\,v=10i+19j,\,a=2i+3j,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 10i+19j & =-6i-5j+(2i+3j)t \\ 16i+24j & =(2i+3j)t \\ 16i+24j & =2ti+3tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}16=2t \\ 24=3t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=8\,\text{s}.
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=-i+7j,\,u=2i-5j,\,v=3i+2j

into the equation above, we can attempt to solve for $t,$ as follows:

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
canonical_examples.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(\mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\textrm{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}^2,$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
\mathbf u = \mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = 2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} .
$$

Therefore, after $t = 5 \, \textrm{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(i-4j)+(2i+j)(5) \\  & =(i-4j)+(10i+5j) \\  & =(11i+j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
\mathbf{u} = 4\mathbf{i}, \qquad

t =3

$$

canonical_examples.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{km/h}^2.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\textrm{h}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})  \, \textrm{km/h}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}, \qquad
\mathbf{u} = -\mathbf{i} -\mathbf{j}, \qquad
\mathbf{v} = 3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j}
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 3i+7j & =(-i-j)+(i+2j)t \\ 4i+8j & =(i+2j)t \\ 4i+8j & =ti+2tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=t \\ 8=2t\end{aligned}
$$
